mount.note: The GY-521 (MPU6050) sits with its Y axis up: gravity reads +9.8 on Y (2026-09-07), so a roll of +90 deg maps the chip's Y onto base_link's Z; its Y gyro is the yaw rate. The board publishes base_link -> imu_link from this, and its C++ bridge applies the same rotation to every reading before publishing (base_bridge.cpp to_base_axes, imu_up_axis y, frame_id base_link), so a base_link reading is already in the robot's axes; the laptop's depth node applies this mount only to a reading published in another frame, never to a base_link one (it would be rotated twice).
